recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It keeps the original FHIR-7502 ordering clarification, aligns narrative and conformance source after FHIR-24878, and needs no additional core follow-up for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-7502 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core List change request asking whether List item order is preserved, how order can be reconstructed without an item sequence number, and whether orderedBy merely names the ordering criterion. The accepted resolution was to add clarifying notes.
initial_application: The issue was directly applied by git commit 884699db409ff12d65bfbbdd2976a9abb381046b, imported from svn revision 5596, which added the List Order narrative in source/list/list-notes.xml. The List resource remains active in source/fhir.ini, so that narrative is in current build scope.
additional_context: A later Published/Persuasive decision, FHIR-24878, added List.entry.orderMeaning: order has no meaning unless specifically asserted by List.orderedBy. The linked Zulip thread and FHIR-I 2020-03-23 minutes show this later issue was about how implementations identify ordered collections and was approved 7-0-0. The combined branch already contains a separate FHIR-24878 audit commit, so this worker did not publish another one.
reconciliation: Changed source/list/list-notes.xml to say orderedBy gives item order a defined meaning, and when orderedBy is absent this specification does not assign a defined meaning even though entries remain represented in literal order. This removes the stale statement that order meaning may be implicit, which conflicted with List.entry.orderMeaning.
source_changes: source/list/list-notes.xml: replaced the statement that order meaning may be implicit with wording that absent orderedBy the specification assigns no defined meaning, while entries remain represented in literal order.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive List issue added the active List.entry.orderMeaning rule that narrowed the older FHIR-7502 narrative; already represented on the combined branch.
